brand.name: Leland
taglines: Get there, with the people who’ve been there.

pitch.headline: Get there, with the people who've been there.
pitch.oneliner: Leland Community is where you follow people who've already done what you're trying to do, and learn from them every day. It's free.
pitch.core: most people don't get this kind of access until years into their careers. Now you get it as a sophomore, no network required.

three.title: Real people who've done it
three.say: Experts post with real names and verified backgrounds: former bankers, PMs at Google and Salesforce, consultants, HBS admits. Sometimes it's a senior who landed at Bain last month, and that counts too.
three.why: Forums are anonymous and LinkedIn is a highlight reel. This is the real story from someone who lived it.

three.title: A feed built around your goal
three.say: You follow the path you're on, not the people you already know.
three.why: Your network shouldn't decide what advice you get.

three.title: Go deeper when you're ready
three.say: Catch a livestream, ask in an AMA, or book a call with an expert from their profile.
three.why: Learning in the feed is free. If you need more, it's one tap away.

sound.d: This is a launch, so let the energy show. Back every bit of hype with something real: a specific company, a real question, a real person.
We sound welcoming when we invite people in: "come ask," "the door's open," "send this to someone who needs it." We don't need community-speak to get there.

sound.t: Lead with learning from people who've done it.
sound.d: Meeting peers is a nice bonus, but it's not the headline.

sound.t: Keep the product human, not techy.
sound.d: Don't describe the feed as AI-powered, algorithmic or personalized. Say "your feed is built around where you're trying to go." AI Builder posts can talk about AI freely, since that's what those builders are making.

sound.t: Don't name LinkedIn as the comparison in public posts.
sound.d: Most of these posts will run on LinkedIn. Show the difference and let readers draw the comparison.

use: follow, learn, ask, been there, real, open, free, every day
"your feed is built around your goal"
specific names: Google, Goldman, McKinsey, Bain, HBS
avoid: platform, ecosystem, unlock, empower, journey, revolutionize

launched.lede: Leland Community is a feed where you follow people who've already done what you're trying to do, and learn from them every day.
bullets: Experts with real names and verified backgrounds post what they know: how they got in, what they'd do differently, what the job is actually like.
Your feed is built around where you're trying to go: consulting, finance, product, tech and startups, MBA and more.
Livestreams and AMAs live in the feed, so you can ask questions in real time.
When you want to go deeper, you can book a call with an expert right from their profile.
AI Builder Program students and grads have their own space to share what they build.
It's free on iOS, Android and web.
why: Most ambitious students don't know anyone who has done the thing they want to do. The sophomore who just heard about product management doesn't have a PM in the family. Networking feels like a black box, and LinkedIn isn't built for someone with 200 connections.
So they guess. They read anonymous threads and polished highlight reels and try to piece it together.

The people who could answer their questions already exist, and thousands of them are on Leland. Community puts what they know in front of you every day, years before you'd normally have that kind of network.
who: Core persona: an ambitious sophomore in the business school at a top-50 university, eyeing consulting, finance, product or tech, who knows they need to network but doesn't know where to start.

Write for them first, but don't exclude anyone. The product is open, and existing clients, grad school applicants, career switchers and AI Builder Program grads are all welcome. See Community ICP & GTM Plan (Oct 2026) for the full thinking.

faq.a: Yes. Following, reading and asking questions are free. Booking a 1:1 call with an expert is paid.
Leland experts with real names and verified backgrounds, plus people a step or two ahead of you who just landed where you want to go.
No. It's for anyone figuring out their next move: consulting, finance, product, tech, grad school, AI and more.

guardrails: Post on Oct 15 or later. Nothing before.
Lead with learning from people who've done it. Meeting peers is a bonus, not the headline.
Say "experts post with real names," not "every post."
Real stories beat generic lines. If you have one, use it.
Don't call the Community product AI-powered.
Don't make up numbers, and don't quote the sample numbers in the graphics as real.
CTA: "Come ask" or "Follow along," with a link to the App Store, Google Play or web.

posts.title: The announcement
posts.idea: say what launched, who's on it, and that it's free.

posts.title: Real answers from people who've done it
posts.idea: let the visual do the talking. Real questions, answered by people who've already been through it.
posts.works: Learn video, or the "Ask anything. Get real answers." hero

posts.title: "I wish I'd had this"
posts.tag: a moment from your own path
posts.idea: a short personal moment (the recruiting season you guessed your way through, the person you wish you'd known) and why this would have changed it. The more specific the memory, the better.
posts.works: "Learn from people who've done it" or "Your next move starts here" hero, or the Learn video
posts.text:
In college I didn't know a single person who'd [done the thing you wanted to do]. So I guessed.

Starting today, students don't have to. Leland Community lets you follow people who've been there and learn from them every day. {link}

posts.title: Question → answer
posts.idea: a real question someone is asking, then the person who's already lived the answer.
posts.works: a card pair as a two-image post (Kevin → Marcus, or Amara → Alex), or the "Ask anything" hero on its own
posts.text:
"Is it actually possible to land a FAANG job if you've never had an internship?"

On Leland Community, you can ask the people who did it. {link}

posts.title: Your network, before you have one
posts.idea: speak to students who don't have connections yet. Name the companies and paths they're curious about.
posts.works: People video, "Your next move starts here" or "Find your people" hero, or the Sofia / James cards
posts.text:
Sophomores: you don't need to know someone at Google to learn how people get into Google.

Follow consultants, bankers and PMs who broke in at places like Google, Meta and Goldman. They post what worked, what didn't, and what the job is actually like. It's free. {link}

posts.title: The best thing I've seen in the feed
posts.idea: screenshot one great post or answer from the feed and say why it stuck with you. This one gets better every week as the feed fills up.
posts.works: your screenshot, or the Maya Chen card as an example
posts.text:
"Your resume matters less than your ability to tell the same story out loud in 60 seconds."

That's the kind of take showing up in Leland Community this week. Come see what else people are saying. {link}

posts.title: Come ask me
posts.tag: for experts and anyone with a story
posts.idea: if you know something people want to learn (a path, a school, a job), invite them to follow you and bring their questions.
posts.works: your own profile or livestream card (the Ben Carter card shows what that looks like)
posts.text: I'm posting on Leland Community now. If you're [recruiting for consulting / breaking into PM / applying to MBA programs], follow along and bring your questions. {link}

posts.title: Behind the build
posts.idea: a proud, human look at the team that shipped it. Celebrate the people, then point to the product.
posts.works: a team photo, the People video, or the "Accomplish your goals, together" hero
posts.text: Our team has been heads down on this for months, and it's live today. Leland Community puts our experts, livestreams and AMAs in one feed. Really proud of this crew. Go take a look: {link}

posts.title: Win the day
posts.idea: celebrate the everyday progress that happens in the feed: the early interview, the practice test that finally clicked, the offer. Keep it upbeat and point to the experts cheering people on.
posts.works: Momentum video, or the "Accomplish your goals, together" hero
